title: The constant sheaf of sets with value E is represented by the disjoint union of E copies of the base
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ a set. Let $U_E=\coprod_{e\in E}U$ be the coproduct of copies of $U$ indexed by $E$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with coprojections $\iota_e:U\to U_E$, and let $\pi:U_E\to U$ be the codiagonal, the morphism with $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_U$ for all $e\in E$; regard $U_E$ as a $U$-scheme through $\pi$. Let $h_{U_E}$ be the presheaf of sets on the small etale site $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] given by $h_{U_E}(s:W\to U)=\operatorname{Mor}_U(W,U_E)$, restriction being composition, and let $\underline E$ be the constant sheaf of sets on $U_{\Et}$ with value $E$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with its canonical map $\eta$ from the constant presheaf $W\mapsto E$. Then $h_{U_E}$ is a sheaf of sets on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], and the morphism of presheaves $c$ from the constant presheaf $W\mapsto E$ to $h_{U_E}$, $c_{(W,s)}(e)=\iota_e\circ s$, factors as $c=\varphi\circ\eta$ for a unique morphism of sheaves $\varphi:\underline E\to h_{U_E}$, and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. (For $E=\varnothing$, $U_\varnothing$ is the empty scheme.)

source.place: Remark Tag 03P5 (remark-constant-locally-constant-maps, lines 2437-2456), stated there for an abstract group $G$, the group structure playing no role; with Groupoids, Example Tag 03YW (groupoids-example-constant-group) and Lemma Tag 03O3 (lemma-representable-sheaf-fpqc). Used in the proof of Lemma Tag 03RV (lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant, lines 9993-10023).

proof.text: *Step 1 ($h_{U_E}$ is a sheaf and $c$ is a morphism of presheaves).* Regard $U_E$ as a $U$-scheme through $\pi$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. By [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] (Stacks Lemma Tag 03O3, applied with $T=U$ and $X=U_E$), the presheaf $h_{U_E}(W,s)=\operatorname{Mor}_U(W,U_E)$ is a sheaf of sets on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. The map $c_{(W,s)}(e)=\iota_e\circ s$ lands in $\operatorname{Mor}_U(W,U_E)$ since $\pi\circ\iota_e\circ s=s$, and it is natural: for a morphism $g:(W',s')\to(W,s)$ of $U_{\Et}$ (so $s\circ g=s'$) we get $c_{(W,s)}(e)\circ g=\iota_e\circ s'=c_{(W',s')}(e)$, which is the restriction of $c_{(W,s)}(e)$ along $g$ in $h_{U_E}$ and the image of $e$ under the identity restriction map of the constant presheaf.

source.place: Remark Tag 03P5: 'By Lemma 03O3 any representable presheaf satisfies the sheaf condition for the $\tau$-topology'; Lemma Tag 03O3 (lemma-representable-sheaf-fpqc)

proof.text: *Step 2 (sections of $h_{U_E}$ are locally constant: Zariski-local description).* Let $(W,s)$ be an object of $U_{\Et}$ and $f\in h_{U_E}(W,s)$. By [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen] (a), the sets $W_e=f^{-1}(\iota_e(U))$, $e\in E$, form an $E$-indexed clopen decomposition of $W$, and with $j_e:W_e\to W$ the inclusion of the open subscheme, $f\circ j_e=\iota_e\circ s\circ j_e=c_{(W_e,s\circ j_e)}(e)$. Each $j_e$ is an open immersion, hence etale, and $s\circ j_e$ is etale as a composite of etale morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; so $(W_e,s\circ j_e)$ is an object of $U_{\Et}$ and, the $W_e$ covering $W$, $\mathcal W_f=\{j_e:W_e\to W\}_{e\in E}$ is a covering of $(W,s)$ in $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] on whose members $f$ restricts to the image of a constant: $f|_{W_e}=c_{W_e}(e)$. Two facts about this covering: (i) for $e\ne e'$ the fibre product $Z=W_e\times_WW_{e'}$ (computed in schemes, [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]) is empty, since every point of $Z$ maps to a point of $W_e\cap W_{e'}=\varnothing$; (ii) for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $U_{\Et}$ and every empty object $Z$, $\mathcal G(Z)$ has exactly one element, because the empty family is a covering of $Z$ and the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] makes $\mathcal G(Z)$ the equalizer of two maps between empty products, i.e. a one-point set. Finally, for $f=c_{(W,s)}(e_0)$ part (c) of [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen] gives $W_{e_0}=W$ and $W_e=\varnothing$ for $e\ne e_0$; and for a morphism $g:(W',s')\to(W,s)$ the decomposition of $f\circ g$ is $((f\circ g)^{-1}(\iota_e(U)))_e=(g^{-1}(W_e))_e$.

source.place: Groupoids, Example Tag 03YW: $G_S(T)=\{f:T\to G\text{ locally constant}\}$; Etale Cohomology, Remark Tag 03P5: 'This Zariski sheaf is representable by the group scheme $G_S$'

proof.text: *Step 3 ($(h_{U_E},c)$ has the universal property of the sheafification of the constant presheaf $P_E:W\mapsto E$).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $U_{\Et}$ and $\alpha:P_E\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of presheaves, so $\alpha_W(e)|_{W'}=\alpha_{W'}(e)$ for every morphism $W'\to W$. Existence: for $f\in h_{U_E}(W)$ take the covering $\{W_e\to W\}_e$ of Step 2 and the sections $t_e=\alpha_{W_e}(e)\in\mathcal G(W_e)$. They agree on overlaps: on $Z=W_e\times_WW_e$ both pullbacks of $t_e$ equal $\alpha_Z(e)$ by naturality of $\alpha$; on $W_e\times_WW_{e'}$, $e\ne e'$, which is empty, $\mathcal G$ has one element (Step 2 (i), (ii)). By the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] there is a unique $\beta_W(f)\in\mathcal G(W)$ with $\beta_W(f)|_{W_e}=\alpha_{W_e}(e)$ for all $e$. Naturality of $\beta$: for $g:W'\to W$, the decomposition of $f\circ g$ is $W'_e=g^{-1}(W_e)$ (Step 2), and on $W'_e$ both $\beta_W(f)|_{W'}$ and $\beta_{W'}(f\circ g)$ restrict to $\alpha_{W'_e}(e)$ (the first because $W'_e\to W'\to W$ factors through $W_e$ and $\alpha_{W_e}(e)|_{W'_e}=\alpha_{W'_e}(e)$); as $\{W'_e\to W'\}$ is a covering, they are equal by the uniqueness half of the sheaf condition. $\beta\circ c=\alpha$: for $f=c_W(e_0)$ the decomposition is $W_{e_0}=W$, $W_e=\varnothing$ otherwise (Step 2), so $\beta_W(c_W(e_0))=\beta_W(c_W(e_0))|_W=\alpha_W(e_0)$. Uniqueness: if $\beta':h_{U_E}\to\mathcal G$ satisfies $\beta'\circ c=\alpha$, then for $f\in h_{U_E}(W)$, using $f|_{W_e}=c_{W_e}(e)$ (Step 2) and naturality of $\beta'$, $\beta'_W(f)|_{W_e}=\beta'_{W_e}(c_{W_e}(e))=\alpha_{W_e}(e)=\beta_W(f)|_{W_e}$ for all $e$, so $\beta'_W(f)=\beta_W(f)$ by the sheaf condition. Thus every morphism from $P_E$ to a sheaf factors uniquely through $c$, which is the defining property of a sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] (the Zariski covering $\{W_e\to W\}$ already suffices, as in the source).

source.place: Remark Tag 03P5: 'the sheafification $\underline G$ of the constant presheaf associated to $G$ in the Zariski topology of the site already gives $\Gamma(U,\underline G)=\{$Zariski locally constant maps $U\to G\}$ ... hence we conclude that the Zariski sheafification $\underline G$ above is also the $\tau$-sheafification' (the argument written out for sets; the group structure plays no role)

proof.text: *Step 4 (the factorization $\varphi$ and its invertibility).* By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] $\underline E$ with $\eta:P_E\to\underline E$ is the sheafification of $P_E$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; since $h_{U_E}$ is a sheaf (Step 1), $c$ factors as $c=\varphi\circ\eta$ for a unique $\varphi:\underline E\to h_{U_E}$ (morphisms of sheaves being morphisms of presheaves, [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]). By Step 3 applied to $\mathcal G=\underline E$ and $\alpha=\eta$ there is $\psi:h_{U_E}\to\underline E$ with $\psi\circ c=\eta$. Then $(\psi\circ\varphi)\circ\eta=\psi\circ c=\eta=\mathrm{id}\circ\eta$, so $\psi\circ\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{\underline E}$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of $\eta$; and $(\varphi\circ\psi)\circ c=\varphi\circ\eta=c=\mathrm{id}\circ c$, so $\varphi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}_{h_{U_E}}$ by the uniqueness in Step 3 (with $\mathcal G=h_{U_E}$, $\alpha=c$). Hence $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. For $E=\varnothing$ nothing changes: $U_\varnothing$ is the empty scheme and all steps apply verbatim (the decompositions are empty families, existing only over empty $W$).

source.place: Remark Tag 03P5, last sentence: the Zariski sheafification, being representable, is the $\tau$-sheafification

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks Remark 03P5 for sets (the group structure of 03P5/03YW plays no role). Step 1: h_{U_E} is an etale sheaf by lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf (03O3), c is natural. Step 2: by the new node lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen (set version of 03YW: U-morphisms W -> U_E are E-indexed clopen decompositions of W), every section f is c(e) on the members of the Zariski covering {f^{-1}(V_e) -> W} (open immersions etale, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation); overlaps for e != e' are empty and sheaves take one value on empty objects. Step 3: (h_{U_E}, c) satisfies the universal property of the sheafification of the constant presheaf (existence by gluing alpha(e) over that covering, naturality, uniqueness). Step 4: phi exists by the universal property of eta and is an isomorphism by the two uniqueness statements. Statement unchanged. The existing lem-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme-morphism-clopen states the 03YW bijection only for an abelian group E with the group-scheme structure, so it was not cited for a set E; lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant is the abelian-group analogue (it uses lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local; here the universal property is checked directly, which needs no local description of sheafification).
